title: Bipolar mixed and agitated dysphoric states
bottleneck: Mixed states, combining depressive and manic features with agitation, carry the highest suicide risk in bipolar disorder and respond poorly to standard treatments: antidepressants can worsen agitation, and the evidence for mood stabilizers in mixed presentations is thin. Diagnostic recognition itself is inconsistent.
why_it_blocks: The most lethal presentation of bipolar disorder is also the least treatable and least studied. Mixed states concentrate suicide risk precisely where the pharmacology is weakest.
current_state: Atypical antipsychotics are the mainstay for acute mixed episodes based on limited data. ECT is used in refractory cases. Dedicated trials for mixed features remain rare. Mixed features are now a DSM specifier rather than a separate episode type, yet treatment trials still enroll predominantly pure presentations, leaving the highest-risk group understudied.
